theoremCandidate.spectralProjectors: For real reciprocal sources, each resolved state class with amplitude vector v_n=(<n|O_g|0>,<n|O_H|0>) contributes a positive rank-one projector v_n v_n^T to the spectral measure.
theoremCandidate.projectiveCoordinate: When the Higgs amplitude is nonzero, only the ratio r_n=v_g/v_H fixes the projector direction; a vanishing Higgs amplitude is the projective point at infinity.
theoremCandidate.vandermondeCriterion: For three finite ratios r1,r2,r3, the determinant of their coordinates (r_i^2,1,sqrt(2)r_i) is sqrt(2)(r2-r1)(r3-r1)(r3-r2). Thus their projectors span H2(R) exactly when the ratios are pairwise distinct.
theoremCandidate.physicalQualification: Distinct projector directions give linear span. An open physical image additionally requires independently variable nonnegative weights, obtained for example from separated thresholds, controls or selection rules.
theoremCandidate.complexPhaseBoundary: If amplitudes do not admit one common real structure, the natural carrier is H2(C); phase alignment or an antiunitary symmetry is an additional gate for H2(R).
